data.description:
## Problem
The scheduled Test Suite (mirror) Windows sweep reports `ValueError: the environment variable is longer than 32767 characters` in two tests around run 33426859481. Windows caps each environment variable at 32767 characters; some test or subprocess helper appears to pass an oversized payload through `env`.

## Plan
1. Inspect the failing CI log and identify the exact tests/helpers setting the long environment variable.
2. Classify legitimacy: if this is a test-harness-only payload transport, fix the harness to pass large data via a file/stdin/in-process seam; if it is a product path a real Windows user can hit, fix the product path. Escalate if an authoritative design says this behavior is intentional.
3. Add a RED test that simulates the Windows env-var cap deterministically on macOS and fails for the same `ValueError` mechanism before the fix.
4. Apply the smallest fix that avoids oversized Windows env vars without weakening test coverage or adding dependencies.
5. Run the focused test, sandboxed mutation check, `make lint`, and the default suite before Gerrit.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The exact failing tests/helpers from run 33426859481 are identified in the RCA.
- [ ] A local macOS test simulates the Windows 32767-character env-var cap and is RED on current code for the right reason.
- [ ] The fixed path avoids passing oversized payloads through a single environment variable.
- [ ] The RCA comment cites the legitimacy verdict, caller/sibling sweep, and caused-by attribution.
- [ ] Gerrit change is submitted only after `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1`.
data.title: Windows sweep hits 32767-character environment variable limit in tests
